blocks.text: READ: Follow Inquirer Sports’ special coverage of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 Japan cycling queen Yumi Kajihara broke down after her latest Asian Games gold as she dedicated victory to her brother, who died of cancer this year, saying: “He’s here with me.” Kajihara claimed her third consecutive omnium gold at the Izu Velodrome on Friday and dissolved into tears as she talked about how her younger brother Hyogo had helped her cope with some dark moments. “After I missed a medal at the Paris Olympics (2024) I was really depressed,” said the 29-year-old Kajihara, the first woman cyclist from Japan […]...
